candidates.source_description: Saint Agatha was a young Christian woman martyred in Catania, Sicily, around 251 AD, and she remains the city’s patron saint. In the 11th century, her relics were taken to Constantinople by the Byzantines, but on August 17, 1126, they were brought back to Catania in a celebrated return. Since 1376, her skull and upper body have been kept inside an ornate silver reliquary bust in Catania Cathedral.
